narrative: Material PL1__M0614FA1 exhibits lumpy but consistently non-zero demand (CV=0.40, 98.5% non-zero days) with no detectable trend over the observation period. Lead times show moderate variability (CV=0.34) after removal of one extreme outlier (9201.55 days). The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is selected because it balances holding and ordering costs optimally under these conditions, with EOQ batch sizing reducing annual orders from ~173 to ~25 and safety stock increased to statistically cover 95% of demand-during-lead-time scenarios. Storage capacity remains unconstrained at 74.4% utilisation.
warnings: Lead time outlier removed: 9201.55 days (data entry error suspected)
Safety stock increased from SAP baseline of 642 to statistically derived 1230 units
Safety lead time recommended to REDUCE from 4.0 to 2.67 days

research_insights.selection_rationale: With consistent non-zero demand and moderate lead time variability, a continuous-review reorder-point policy with fixed EOQ batch size is the most cost-efficient choice. It avoids the overhead of periodic review while capturing full EOQ savings through infrequent large replenishments.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (6,048 / 8,131 units = 74.4%). No capacity-driven order reduction required. If demand surges above the 99th percentile concurrently with maximum lead time, peak stock could approach 7,200 units — still within limit.
